newsitem.title: USA: CFTC chief-Greenspan has no position on reform yet.
newsitem.headline: CFTC chief-Greenspan has no position on reform yet.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairwoman Brooksley Born said Friday that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan assured her that he has not yet taken a postion on CFTC reform.
"He has told me that he has not taken a position on the pending bills," Born told reporters after addressing a derivatives conference.
She said Greenspan's remarks last month were incorrectly interpreted as supporting Senate and House bills that would strip the CFTC of much of its jurisdiction.
"He (Greenspan) was talking about policy, not about specific legislation," Born added.

Greenspan said in a speech several weeks ago that he supported a free market approach to oversight of financial exchanges. Born said the remarks gave "enormous impetus" to the pending CFTC legislation.

Born also said that the Securities and Exchange Commission supports the CFTC view that the agency must retain regulatory oversight of U.S. futures and options traders to prevent fraud and manipulation.
She said a number of end-users in the agricultural community were also supporting the CFTC position.
The CFTC is interested in "opening a dialogue" with the major U.S. exchanges to find a compromise that would lessen some of the agency's regulations but not go as far as the House and Senate bills.

Bills introduced by Sen. Richard Lugar, R-Ind., and Rep. Thomas Ewing, R-Ill., would eliminate CFTC oversight of so-called professional market traders with a net worth of $1 million or more. The bills would also eliminate exchange audit trails, large trader reporting and various exchange recordkeeping requirements.
